verdicts.trueWording: conjured an entire planet into vivid existence

Byline 'By Michael Chabon / November 20, 2019' present. Full sentence: 'With nothing but language-lines on paper, properly configured-Ursula K. Le Guin conjured an entire planet into vivid existence, detailed and plausible from its flora to its weather to the dialects and ceremonies of its inhabitants.' Every limb supported, including 'nothing but lines on paper' ('with nothing but language-lines on paper, properly configured').

verdicts.trueWording: weaving each place's contradictions, tensions, mores, and rites into satisfyingly detailed portraits

Sentence: 'You may begin as a stranger in these strange lands, but soon take up residence inside them thanks to Le Guin's brilliance at weaving each place's contradictions, tensions, mores, and rites into satisfyingly detailed portraits of authentic extraterrestrial societies.' verdicts.trueWording: Perhaps Left Hand's most famous sentence ... 'The king was pregnant'
verdicts.note: Same raw fetch. Page: 'Perhaps Left Hand's most famous sentence appears in Chapter 8, when Argaven, the monarch of Karhide ..., finds himself with child. "The king was pregnant," Genly Ai writes in a field report...'. Quote verbatim. Two minor divergences that do not unseat a limb: Vest hedges with 'Perhaps' where the claim states it flatly, and 'four-word' is the verifier's count of the quoted line (He/is/... -> 'The king was pregnant' = 4 words), not the page's own wording.

verdicts.trueWording: 'He is done with doing.' ... no matter how lovely that sentence is
verdicts.note: Live reactormag.com fetched raw (HTTP 200, curl); comments are server-rendered in the HTML. Commenter 'Msb' (6 years ago) on 'Introducing the Ursula K. Le Guin Reread' (Sean Guynes, 22 Jan 2020) writes: 'Le Guin was writing masterworks well after the 1970s. "He is done with doing." Except he wasn't, of course, no matter how lovely that sentence is.' Quote verbatim; the line is five words (He/is/done/with/doing) and is Le Guin's (Earthsea); 'lovely' is the commenter's own word, though applied concessively.

verdicts.trueWording: There was no sense of islands in a lonely ocean
verdicts.note: PDF fetched as binary (HTTP 200, 4.96 MB) and text-extracted with pypdf (54 pages). Article "'Earthsea' and 'Tales From Earthsea' By Terry Morris" begins p. 27 of the issue; the quote is on PDF page 30: 'It was particularly surprising that most of the scenes were set firmly on land. There was no sense of islands in a lonely ocean, no sense of the sea as a constant element in people's lives...'. Quote verbatim, and the fault is aimed at the Studio Ghibli Tales From Earthsea film. Two metadata nits outside the claim sentence: the chunk's page field says p. 31 (actual PDF page 30, printed folio 29/30), and the fanzine's cover reads 'February 2010' while its colophon reads 'No 11, February 2009' as the chunk has it.
